# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #803._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/scm.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same `{}`-swallow as AC3c — but on a line this diff touches**

The PR fixes AC3c by logging `fetchError.message` instead of a raw Error (the host console renders an Error as `{}`), yet this modified `console.warn` still passes the raw `e`:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e);
```

Apply the same content extraction for log-hygiene consistency:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e && e.message ? e.message : String(e));
```

(Also note `js/common/gitOps.js:64` and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js:64/311` already use the `e.message || String(e)` pattern — this line is the outlier.)

---

### Thread 3 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: knob name now contradicts what it writes — document the override path**

`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment` now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` (correct per AC3b — the written status should match the phase). But the name/behavior mismatch is now permanent, and there is a migration note worth surfacing:

- Projects that enabled this knob **without** an `In Rework` status in their Jira workflow will now get a failed (warned, non-fatal) transition on every rework leg, where the old `In Development` write succeeded. The escape hatch exists — `config.jira.statuses.IN_REWORK` remaps the target — but nothing tells them to use it.
- Consider documenting this in the config docs (and optionally aliasing the knob as `markReworkActive` with back-compat reading of the old name) in a follow-up, so the next reader doesn't assume a bug.

Not blocking: opt-in knob, failure is caught, and the PR description discloses the behavior change.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/common/gitOps.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the catch-all treats *any* quiet-diff failure as "staged changes"**

Only exit code 1 means "the merge staged changes". Any other failure of `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` (corrupt index, git error) also lands here and prints the "base branch changes staged" claim — the same class of inaccurate log line AC3a set out to remove. The logic is strictly better than before (no-op merges now correctly report "already up to date"), so this is polish only:

```js
} catch (eQuiet) {
    // exit 1 → the merge staged base changes; anything else is a git error,
    // not evidence of staged content
    if (String(eQuiet && eQuiet.message).indexOf('COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=1') === -1) {
        console.warn('git diff --cached --quiet failed (assuming staged):', eQuiet && eQuiet.message ? eQuiet.message : String(eQuiet));
    }
    stagedChanges = true;
}
```

Note the GraalJS `cmd()` helper surfaces exit codes as `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=N` inside the thrown message (see the test mocks), so the exit code is recoverable if you want to split the paths later.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 803
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/803
- **Title**: gh-802 [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-802` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +229
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:09:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T21:23:08Z

## PR Description

Closes #802
### Root Cause

`js/common/scm.js` passed `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing) to `github_get_pr_diff_text`, but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch failed on every call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`, 4/4 in fa run 37806292238) and the ~4-step fallback chain silently did the real work. The same forensic review surfaced three log-hygiene defects (false "base branch changes staged" line, stale `In Development` status write during rework, questions-fetch error rendered as `{}`).

### Fix

- `js/common/scm.js`: `github_get_pr_diff_text` now receives `pullRequestId` at both call sites (`getDiffText`, `getPrDiff`). The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it.
- `js/common/gitOps.js` (AC3a): `detectMergeConflicts` probes `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after a clean merge and logs "branch already up to date" instead of the false "base branch changes staged" on a no-op merge.
- `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` (AC3b): the opt-in rework-active transition (`markReworkInDevelopment`) now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` — the actual phase — instead of the stale `In Development`. Knob name unchanged (config compatibility).

# gh-802: [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it

## Description

## Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

### Thread 2 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same `{}`-swallow as AC3c — but on a line this diff touches**

The PR fixes AC3c by logging `fetchError.message` instead of a raw Error (the host console renders an Error as `{}`), yet this modified `console.warn` still passes the raw `e`:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e);
```

Apply the same content extraction for log-hygiene consistency:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e && e.message ? e.message : String(e));
```

(Also note `js/common/gitOps.js:64` and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js:64/311` already use the `e.message || String(e)` pattern — this line is the outlier.)

### Thread 3 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: knob name now contradicts what it writes — document the override path**

`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment` now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` (correct per AC3b — the written status should match the phase). But the name/behavior mismatch is now permanent, and there is a migration note worth surfacing:

- Projects that enabled this knob **without** an `In Rework` status in their Jira workflow will now get a failed (warned, non-fatal) transition on every rework leg, where the old `In Development` write succeeded. The escape hatch exists — `config.jira.statuses.IN_REWORK` remaps the target — but nothing tells them to use it.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the catch-all treats *any* quiet-diff failure as "staged changes"**

Only exit code 1 means "the merge staged changes". Any other failure of `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` (corrupt index, git error) also lands here and prints the "base branch changes staged" claim — the same class of inaccurate log line AC3a set out to remove. The logic is strictly better than before (no-op merges now correctly report "already up to date"), so this is polish only:

```js

    // exit 1 → the merge staged base changes; anything else is a git error,

```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

- **PR #**: 803
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/803
- **Title**: gh-802 [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-802` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +229
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:09:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T21:23:08Z

## PR Description

Closes #802
### Root Cause

`js/common/scm.js` passed `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing) to `github_get_pr_diff_text`, but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch failed on every call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`, 4/4 in fa run 37806292238) and the ~4-step fallback chain silently did the real work. The same forensic review surfaced three log-hygiene defects (false "base branch changes staged" line, stale `In Development` status write during rework, questions-fetch error rendered as `{}`).

### Fix

- `js/common/scm.js`: `github_get_pr_diff_text` now receives `pullRequestId` at both call sites (`getDiffText`, `getPrDiff`). The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it.
- `js/common/gitOps.js` (AC3a): `detectMergeConflicts` probes `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after a clean merge and logs "branch already up to date" instead of the false "base branch changes staged" on a no-op merge.
- `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` (AC3b): the opt-in rework-active transition (`markReworkInDevelopment`) now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` — the actual phase — instead of the stale `In Development`. Knob name unchanged (config compatibility).
- `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` (AC3c): the questions-fetch failure logs `fetchError.message`/`String(fetchError)` — the host console renders a raw Error object as `{}`.
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (AC3d): no code change needed — a success-path test now pins that `agent:rework` is removed exactly once per completed rework.

### Test Coverage

- `test_githubHelpers.js`: arg-name pins for `pullRequestId` (AC1) + 1-call/0-fallback count test (AC2) — failed before the fix, pass after.
- `test_gitOps.js` (AC3a), `test_preCliReworkSetup.js` (AC3b), `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js` (AC3c): wording/state tests — RED before, GREEN after.
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js` (AC3d): single-removal invariant pin.
- Full `run_all.json`: 1954 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1949 + 5 new tests).

### Notes

- No breaking changes: the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback and the `markReworkInDevelopment` config knob keep their public names/schemas; only the mis-cased argument and the status value written change.
- PR-anchored reworks (`pr-N`) still skip tracker status moves by design.

## Description

## Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #803._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/scm.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same `{}`-swallow as AC3c — but on a line this diff touches**

The PR fixes AC3c by logging `fetchError.message` instead of a raw Error (the host console renders an Error as `{}`), yet this modified `console.warn` still passes the raw `e`:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e);
```

Apply the same content extraction for log-hygiene consistency:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e && e.message ? e.message : String(e));
```

(Also note `js/common/gitOps.js:64` and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js:64/311` already use the `e.message || String(e)` pattern — this line is the outlier.)

---

### Thread 3 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: knob name now contradicts what it writes — document the override path**

`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment` now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` (correct per AC3b — the written status should match the phase). But the name/behavior mismatch is now permanent, and there is a migration note worth surfacing:

- Projects that enabled this knob **without** an `In Rework` status in their Jira workflow will now get a failed (warned, non-fatal) transition on every rework leg, where the old `In Development` write succeeded. The escape hatch exists — `config.jira.statuses.IN_REWORK` remaps the target — but nothing tells them to use it.
- Consider documenting this in the config docs (and optionally aliasing the knob as `markReworkActive` with back-compat reading of the old name) in a follow-up, so the next reader doesn't assume a bug.

Not blocking: opt-in knob, failure is caught, and the PR description discloses the behavior change.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/common/gitOps.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the catch-all treats *any* quiet-diff failure as "staged changes"**

Only exit code 1 means "the merge staged changes". Any other failure of `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` (corrupt index, git error) also lands here and prints the "base branch changes staged" claim — the same class of inaccurate log line AC3a set out to remove. The logic is strictly better than before (no-op merges now correctly report "already up to date"), so this is polish only:

```js
} catch (eQuiet) {
    // exit 1 → the merge staged base changes; anything else is a git error,
    // not evidence of staged content
    if (String(eQuiet && eQuiet.message).indexOf('COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=1') === -1) {
        console.warn('git diff --cached --quiet failed (assuming staged):', eQuiet && eQuiet.message ? eQuiet.message : String(eQuiet));
    }
    stagedChanges = true;
}
```

Note the GraalJS `cmd()` helper surfaces exit codes as `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=N` inside the thrown message (see the test mocks), so the exit code is recoverable if you want to split the paths later.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 803
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/803
- **Title**: gh-802 [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-802` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +229
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:09:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T21:23:08Z

## PR Description

Closes #802
### Root Cause

`js/common/scm.js` passed `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing) to `github_get_pr_diff_text`, but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch failed on every call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`, 4/4 in fa run 37806292238) and the ~4-step fallback chain silently did the real work. The same forensic review surfaced three log-hygiene defects (false "base branch changes staged" line, stale `In Development` status write during rework, questions-fetch error rendered as `{}`).

### Fix

- `js/common/scm.js`: `github_get_pr_diff_text` now receives `pullRequestId` at both call sites (`getDiffText`, `getPrDiff`). The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it.

# gh-802: [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it

## Description

## Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.
- **AC2** — with the tool mocked to succeed, the fallback chain is not exercised (call-count test: 1 call, 0 fallbacks).
- **AC3** — log-hygiene bundle from the same forensic review, same PR: (a) no false "base branch changes staged" line on an up-to-date merge; (b) the issue status write reflects the actual transition (In Rework, not stale In Development); (c) the questions-fetch error is logged with its content, not swallowed as `{}`; (d) `agent:rework` removal happens once, not twice.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

## References

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```

{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same `{}`-swallow as AC3c — but on a line this diff touches**

The PR fixes AC3c by logging `fetchError.message` instead of a raw Error (the host console renders an Error as `{}`), yet this modified `console.warn` still passes the raw `e`:

```js

```

Apply the same content extraction for log-hygiene consistency:

```js

```

### Thread 3 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: knob name now contradicts what it writes — document the override path**

`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment` now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` (correct per AC3b — the written status should match the phase). But the name/behavior mismatch is now permanent, and there is a migration note worth surfacing:

- Projects that enabled this knob **without** an `In Rework` status in their Jira workflow will now get a failed (warned, non-fatal) transition on every rework leg, where the old `In Development` write succeeded. The escape hatch exists — `config.jira.statuses.IN_REWORK` remaps the target — but nothing tells them to use it.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the catch-all treats *any* quiet-diff failure as "staged changes"**

Only exit code 1 means "the merge staged changes". Any other failure of `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` (corrupt index, git error) also lands here and prints the "base branch changes staged" claim — the same class of inaccurate log line AC3a set out to remove. The logic is strictly better than before (no-op merges now correctly report "already up to date"), so this is polish only:

```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 803
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/803
- **Title**: gh-802 [BUG] scm.js: github_get_pr_diff_text passes pullRequestID (schema wants pullRequestId) — diff fetch fails 100%, fallback masks it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-802` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +229
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:09:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T21:23:08Z

## PR Description

Closes #802
### Root Cause

`js/common/scm.js` passed `pullRequestID` (ADO-era casing) to `github_get_pr_diff_text`, but the runtime tool schema requires `pullRequestId` — so the diff-text fetch failed on every call (`host callback returned invalid JSON`, 4/4 in fa run 37806292238) and the ~4-step fallback chain silently did the real work. The same forensic review surfaced three log-hygiene defects (false "base branch changes staged" line, stale `In Development` status write during rework, questions-fetch error rendered as `{}`).

### Fix

- `js/common/scm.js`: `github_get_pr_diff_text` now receives `pullRequestId` at both call sites (`getDiffText`, `getPrDiff`). The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it.
- `js/common/gitOps.js` (AC3a): `detectMergeConflicts` probes `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` after a clean merge and logs "branch already up to date" instead of the false "base branch changes staged" on a no-op merge.
- `js/preCliReworkSetup.js` (AC3b): the opt-in rework-active transition (`markReworkInDevelopment`) now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` — the actual phase — instead of the stale `In Development`. Knob name unchanged (config compatibility).
- `js/fetchQuestionsToInput.js` (AC3c): the questions-fetch failure logs `fetchError.message`/`String(fetchError)` — the host console renders a raw Error object as `{}`.
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (AC3d): no code change needed — a success-path test now pins that `agent:rework` is removed exactly once per completed rework.

### Test Coverage

- `test_githubHelpers.js`: arg-name pins for `pullRequestId` (AC1) + 1-call/0-fallback count test (AC2) — failed before the fix, pass after.
- `test_gitOps.js` (AC3a), `test_preCliReworkSetup.js` (AC3b), `test_fetchQuestionsToInput.js` (AC3c): wording/state tests — RED before, GREEN after.
- `test_pushReworkChanges.js` (AC3d): single-removal invariant pin.
- Full `run_all.json`: 1954 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1949 + 5 new tests).

### Notes

- No breaking changes: the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback and the `markReworkInDevelopment` config knob keep their public names/schemas; only the mis-cased argument and the status value written change.
- PR-anchored reworks (`pr-N`) still skip tracker status moves by design.

## Description

## Goal — `github_get_pr_diff_text` calls the tool with a wrong argument name, so the diff fetch fails every time (v1)

One sentence: **the scm.js diff fetch passes `pullRequestID` where the Dart tool schema requires `pullRequestId`, so `github_get_pr_diff_text` fails on every call and a ~4×-per-comment fallback chain silently does the real work.**

Forensic evidence (full-log review of fa run 37806292238, rework leg on PR #1420): `github_get_pr_diff_text` failed **4 out of 4 calls** with `host callback returned invalid JSON`, each time papered over by the scm.js fallback that re-fetches the diff another way. The wrong arg is in `js/common/scm.js` (the ADO-era `pullRequestID` casing); every other call site in the repo uses `pullRequestId`. Same review also surfaced the log-hygiene bundle below.

## Why this framing

- The PR pipeline works today only because the fallback hides the failure — hidden 100%-failure paths are how algorithm bugs survive (see the live "no code changes required" incident, #799).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — scm.js calls `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `{ pullRequestId: ... }` (exact schema casing); a unit test pins the arg name.

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — arg-name pin (AC1) + call-count (AC2) in the scm.js tests; wording/state tests for AC3 items in the touched files' suites.
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green.

## Non-goals

- Reworking the fallback chain's existence (it is correct defense-in-depth once AC1/AC2 hold).
- #798 / #799 scope (separate cards).

- Forensic review of fa run 37806292238 (line evidence: `github_get_pr_diff_text` failures ×4 + fallback lines); `js/common/scm.js` diff-fetch section; companion cards #798, #799.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #803._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/scm.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same `{}`-swallow as AC3c — but on a line this diff touches**

The PR fixes AC3c by logging `fetchError.message` instead of a raw Error (the host console renders an Error as `{}`), yet this modified `console.warn` still passes the raw `e`:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e);
```

Apply the same content extraction for log-hygiene consistency:

```js
console.warn('Failed to move ticket to ' + statuses.IN_REWORK + ':', e && e.message ? e.message : String(e));
```

(Also note `js/common/gitOps.js:64` and `js/preCliReworkSetup.js:64/311` already use the `e.message || String(e)` pattern — this line is the outlier.)

---

### Thread 3 — `js/preCliReworkSetup.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: knob name now contradicts what it writes — document the override path**

`config.jira.markReworkInDevelopment` now writes `statuses.IN_REWORK` (correct per AC3b — the written status should match the phase). But the name/behavior mismatch is now permanent, and there is a migration note worth surfacing:

- Projects that enabled this knob **without** an `In Rework` status in their Jira workflow will now get a failed (warned, non-fatal) transition on every rework leg, where the old `In Development` write succeeded. The escape hatch exists — `config.jira.statuses.IN_REWORK` remaps the target — but nothing tells them to use it.
- Consider documenting this in the config docs (and optionally aliasing the knob as `markReworkActive` with back-compat reading of the old name) in a follow-up, so the next reader doesn't assume a bug.

Not blocking: opt-in knob, failure is caught, and the PR description discloses the behavior change.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/common/gitOps.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the catch-all treats *any* quiet-diff failure as "staged changes"**

Only exit code 1 means "the merge staged changes". Any other failure of `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` (corrupt index, git error) also lands here and prints the "base branch changes staged" claim — the same class of inaccurate log line AC3a set out to remove. The logic is strictly better than before (no-op merges now correctly report "already up to date"), so this is polish only:

```js
} catch (eQuiet) {
    // exit 1 → the merge staged base changes; anything else is a git error,
    // not evidence of staged content
    if (String(eQuiet && eQuiet.message).indexOf('COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=1') === -1) {
        console.warn('git diff --cached --quiet failed (assuming staged):', eQuiet && eQuiet.message ? eQuiet.message : String(eQuiet));
    }
    stagedChanges = true;
}
```

Note the GraalJS `cmd()` helper surfaces exit codes as `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=N` inside the thrown message (see the test mocks), so the exit code is recoverable if you want to split the paths later.
